_description: Ground truth data for bill extraction evaluation.

_match_strategy.overall: Per-field scoring with field-appropriate strategies. No single blended accuracy score.

vendor_name.rationale: Handwritten shop names vary in spelling, abbreviation (Provision → Prov.), and inclusion/exclusion of prefixes (Sri, Shri, M/s). Exact match would be too strict for real-world use.

invoice_number.rationale: Invoice numbers are precise identifiers. A wrong number is worse than no number for bookkeeping. No partial credit.

date.rationale: Dates must be correct for accounting. Partial credit (e.g. right month, wrong day) is not useful.

amount.rationale: Total amounts must match for expense reporting. 0.01 tolerance catches floating-point rounding without excusing real errors.

currency.rationale: Binary — either correct or not. For Indian bills, this is almost always INR.

tax_gst.rationale: Tax details have multiple components. Scoring as one binary pass/fail would hide which sub-field fails. Each sub-field scored independently, then averaged.

illegible_fields.rationale: Models can mark fields as illegible. We note this but do not currently score it. A model that admits uncertainty is arguably better than one that hallucinates, but our scoring treats both as incorrect. This is a documented gap.

language.rationale: We track the bill's language to measure multilingual robustness. Some bills are in Malayalam (ml). Not scored in the accuracy table; reported separately.

multilingual_handling.rationale: For non-English bills, ground truth stores the vendor name in the ORIGINAL script (e.g. Malayalam) exactly as printed. This avoids transliteration ambiguity ('Krishna' vs 'Krishnan' vs 'Krsna'). Fuzzy matching is character-based and works on any Unicode script.

absent_fields.method: null in ground truth means the field does not exist on the bill
absent_fields.rationale: Most bills here have NO invoice number. Ground truth = null. A model is correct only if it also returns null. Returning a made-up invoice number is penalized as a hallucination — so invoice_number accuracy measures model honesty, not just reading skill.
